explanation: Maintain an even prefix followed by the odd values already scanned. On finding an even value, swap it into the next even-prefix position; then advance the scan.
timeComplexity: O(n+1): the scan advances once per element.
spaceComplexity: O(1): two indices and temporary swap values; the same array/list is rearranged.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: Before each scan, the processed prefix consists of evens followed by odds. An even value swaps with the first processed odd (or itself), extending the even prefix; an odd value extends the odd region. Each swap preserves all input occurrences. At exhaustion, the invariant covers the whole array.
walkthrough: For [3,2,−5,4], skip the first odd, then swap 2 with 3 to obtain [2,3,−5,4]. Skip −5, then swap 4 with 3 to obtain [2,4,−5,3]. The judge checks even-before-odd order and preserved occurrences, not one unique permutation; the walkthrough expected value true denotes this property check.
edgeCases: Negative odd integers belong in the odd region.
Empty, all-even and all-odd arrays already satisfy the property.
Relative order inside the groups is not required.
